scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: I'm on the IT department head's machine (it_hod) and
I suddenly cannot reach any of the CS department computers (the 192.168.2.x
ones) -- every one of them just times out for me. My own department's
machines are fine, so this machine is not the problem: whatever joins the
departments together is. That is your side, not mine. It worked before and
it does not work now. Take a look and sort it out today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — it_hod (192.168.1.2, lan_it) being unable to reach any CS department machine (192.168.2.x, lan_cs) — cannot be confirmed by any direct evidence in the live lab.

A complete diagnostic pass was performed across all layers. At L2, l2_snapshot scanned all 30 devices and found no duplicate MACs and no down or missing interfaces; every interface on the path (it_hod eth0 → switch0 → router0 eth0/eth1 → switch1 → cs_*) is UP/LOWER_UP with a valid hardware address. At L3, router0's forwarding table contains directly-connected routes for both 192.168.1.0/24 (lan_it, eth0) and 192.168.2.0/24 (lan_cs, eth1), installed as kernel connected routes — correct and stable without OSPF, which is not used here (the topology runs RIP). At the ACL layer, infra_sweep found zero nftables/iptables drop rules on any device. Pressure_sweep found no stress-tool processes, no CPU spikes, and no socket exhaustion anywhere. Service snapshot was not applicable (no web service in the topology).

Live probes confirm the path is healthy today: it_hod reaches cs_hod, cs_lab1, cs_lab2, cs_lab3, and cs_lab4 at 0% loss (TTL=63, confirming the traffic transits router0 as expected), and cs_hod reaches it_hod with equal success. No mechanism — no flap script, no route suppression, no blocking rule — is present that could reproduce the described failure.

Root cause: the symptom is unconfirmed; there is no current or traceable past fault between the IT and CS segments.

Fix: no corrective action is required; the inter-department path via router0 is fully operational. If the user experiences the issue again, capturing the exact time and any concurrent events (interface flap, route withdrawal) would be needed for a fresh investigation.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router0's IT and CS interfaces are up and inter-department routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly verifies router0's IT/CS interfaces are UP, shows connected routes for both subnets, and confirms end-to-end probes with 0% loss, indicating baseline inter-department routing works.

The agent's investigation log contains direct, relevant observations (router routing table, L2/infra snapshots, and multiple successful pings between IT and CS hosts) that substantiate the conclusion; the inference that OSPF alarms are irrelevant because RIP/connected routes are in use is justified and the checks cover L2, L3, ACLs and load. Overall the reasoning is sound and complete for ruling the symptom unconfirmed.
